value.zh: 俄而明宗使人誅延嗣，延嗣暗遁，
value.en: Before long Mingzong sent men to execute Yansi; Yansi fled in secret,
value.literal: Before long Mingzong sent men to execute Yansi; Yansi fled in secret,

value.zh: 〈（《九國志》：明宗即位，忿閹豎輩怙勢擅權，先敕使四方及此遁不出者，皆擒戮之，死者殆盡。）〉
value.en: (Annals of the Nine States records: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, enraged at the eunuchs who relied on power and monopolized authority, he first ordered that eunuch envoys throughout the realm and those in hiding who did not come forth be seized and executed; nearly all were killed.)〉
value.literal: (Annals of the Nine States: When Mingzong took the throne, angry at the eunuch faction that relied on power and usurped authority, he first ordered that eunuch envoys sent to the four directions and those who had fled and did not emerge be captured and executed; nearly all died.)〉

value.zh: 衍之行裝復為篯有，因為富家，積白金萬鎰，藏於窟室。
value.en: Wang Yan's traveling goods again fell into Jian's hands; he thus became a wealthy man, amassing ten thousand ingots of white silver in a hidden vault.
value.literal: Wang Yan's traveling goods again became Jian's possession; he thus became a wealthy house, amassing ten thousand ingots of white silver stored in a hidden vault.

value.zh: 明宗即位，篯進王衍犀、玉帶各二，馬一百五十匹，魏王打球馬七十匹，旋除沂州刺史，入為西衛將軍。
value.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Jian presented two rhinoceros-horn belts and two jade belts from Wang Yan, one hundred fifty horses, and seventy of the Prince of Wei's polo horses; he was soon made prefect of Yizhou and then appointed general of the western guards.
value.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Jian presented two rhinoceros and jade belts each from Wang Yan, one hundred fifty horses, and seventy polo horses of the Prince of Wei; he was soon appointed Yizhou prefect and entered service as western guards general.

value.zh: 高祖即位之明年，加檢校太保，出典密州，未幾，復居環衛。
value.en: In the year after Gaozu's accession he was made acting Grand Guardian, sent out to govern Mizhou, and before long returned to the palace guards.
value.literal: The year after Gaozu ascended, he was made acting Grand Guardian, sent out to govern Mizhou, and soon after returned to the palace guards.

value.zh: 時湖南馬希範與篯有舊，奏朝廷請命篯為使，允之。
value.en: At that time Ma Xifan of Hunan was an old acquaintance of Jian's and memorialized the court to appoint Jian as envoy; the request was granted.
value.literal: At that time Hunan's Ma Xifan was old friends with Jian and memorialized the court to appoint Jian as envoy; approval was granted.

value.zh: 篯密賫蜀之奇貨往售，又獲十餘萬緡以歸。
value.en: Jian secretly took Shu's rare goods to sell and returned with more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.
value.literal: Jian secretly carried Shu rare goods to sell and returned having gained more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.

value.zh: 篯出入以庖者十餘人從行，食皆水陸之珍鮮，厚自奉養，無與為比。
value.en: Whenever Jian went out, more than ten cooks attended him; his meals were delicacies from land and sea. He lived in unrivaled luxury.
value.literal: When going out, Jian was attended by more than ten cooks; his food was delicacies from land and sea; he maintained himself lavishly, unmatched by any other.

value.zh: 少帝嗣位，詔遣往西蕃，及回，以其馬劣，為有司所糾，復當路有不足者，遂有詔征其舊價。
value.en: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, an edict sent him to the western tribes. On his return his horses were judged inferior and the authorities impeached him; moreover those in power who disliked him secured an edict to recover the original purchase price.
value.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, an edict sent him to the western tribes. On his return, because his horses were inferior, he was impeached by the authorities; furthermore there were those in power who bore him ill will, and an edict was issued to collect the old purchase price.

value.zh: 篯上言請貨故京田業，許之，因憤惋成疾而卒。
value.en: Jian memorialized asking to mortgage his former estates in the capital; permission was granted, but indignation and distress brought on illness and he died.
value.literal: Jian memorialized asking to pawn his former capital estates; permission was granted, but resentment and distress brought on illness and he died.

value.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝，姓郭氏，諱威，字文仲，邢州堯山人也。
value.en: Taizu, the Sagely Divine, Respectful, Solemn, Martial, Literary, and Filial Emperor, was of the Guo clan. His personal name was Wei, his courtesy name Wenzhong, and his home was Yao Mountain in Xingzhou.
value.literal: Taizu, the Sagely Divine Respectful Solemn Martial Literary Filial Emperor, bore the surname Guo; his taboo name was Wei, his style Wenzhong, and he was a native of Yao Mountain in Xingzhou.

value.zh: 或云本常氏之子，幼隨母適郭氏，故冒其姓焉。
value.en: Some accounts hold that he was born a Chang, followed his mother into the Guo household as a child, and thereafter bore the Guo surname.
value.literal: Some say he was originally a son of the Chang clan; in youth he followed his mother in marrying into the Guo clan, and therefore took their surname.

value.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：周虢叔之後。）〉
value.en: (According to the Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties, the house descended from Guo Shu of Zhou.)
value.literal: (From the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties": a descendant of Guo Shu of Zhou.)

value.zh: 高祖諱璟，廣順初，追尊為睿和皇帝，廟號信祖，陵曰溫陵；
value.en: The high ancestor, taboo name Jing, was posthumously enthroned as Emperor Ruihe at the opening of Guangshun, with the temple name Xizu and the mausoleum Wenling;
value.literal: The High Ancestor's taboo name was Jing; at the beginning of the Guangshun era he was posthumously honored as Emperor Ruihe, with temple name Xizu and mausoleum called Wenling;

value.zh: 高祖妣張氏，追謚睿恭皇后。
value.en: The High Ancestor's consort, Lady Zhang, received the posthumous title Empress Ruigong.
value.literal: The High Ancestor's consort, née Zhang, was posthumously given the title Empress Ruigong.

value.zh: 曾祖諱諶，漢贈太保，追尊為明憲皇帝，廟號僖祖，陵曰齊陵；
value.en: The great-grandfather, taboo name Chen, was made Grand Guardian under the Han and later raised to Emperor Mingxian, with the temple name Xizu and the mausoleum Qiling;
value.literal: The great-grandfather's taboo name was Chen; the Han posthumously made him Grand Guardian, and he was later honored as Emperor Mingxian, with temple name Xizu and mausoleum Qiling;

value.zh: 曾祖妣鄭國夫人申氏，追謚明孝皇后。
value.en: Lady Shen of Zheng was posthumously styled Empress Mingxiao.
value.literal: The great-grandmother, Lady Shen, Lady of Zheng, was posthumously given the title Empress Mingxiao.

value.zh: 祖諱蘊，漢贈太傅，追尊為翼順皇帝，廟號義祖，陵曰節陵；
value.en: The grandfather, taboo name Yun, was made Grand Tutor under the Han and later raised to Emperor Yishun, with the temple name Yizu and the mausoleum Jieling;
value.literal: The grandfather's taboo name was Yun; the Han posthumously made him Grand Tutor, and he was later honored as Emperor Yishun, with temple name Yizu and mausoleum Jieling;

value.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：溫陵、齊陵、節陵皆無陵所，遙申朝拜。）〉
value.en: (The Institutional Compendium notes that Wenling, Qiling, and Jieling had no physical burial sites; rites were performed by distant petition.)
value.literal: (From the "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties": Wenling, Qiling, and Jieling all had no actual tomb sites; worship was offered from afar.)

value.zh: 祖妣陳國夫人韓氏，追謚翼敬皇后。
value.en: Lady Han of Chen received the posthumous title Empress Yijing.
value.literal: The grandmother, Lady Han, Lady of Chen, was posthumously given the title Empress Yijing.

value.zh: 皇考諱簡，漢贈太師，追尊為章肅皇帝，廟號慶祖，陵曰欽陵；
value.en: His father, taboo name Jian, was made Grand Preceptor under the Han and later raised to Emperor Zhangsu, with the temple name Qingzu and the mausoleum Qinling;
value.literal: The Imperial Father's taboo name was Jian; the Han posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, and he was later honored as Emperor Zhangsu, with temple name Qingzu and mausoleum Qinling;

value.zh: 皇妣燕國夫人王氏，追謚為章德皇后。
value.en: His mother, Lady Wang of Yan, was posthumously styled Empress Zhangde.
value.literal: The Imperial Mother, Lady Wang, Lady of Yan, was posthumously given the title Empress Zhangde.

value.zh: 後以唐天祐元年甲子歲七月二十八日，生帝於堯山之舊宅。
value.en: On the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month in the first Tianyou year of Tang (jiazi), he was born at the family's old home on Yao Mountain.
value.literal: Later, on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month in the first year of Tianyou of Tang, the year jiazi, the Emperor was born at the old residence on Yao Mountain.

value.zh: 載誕之夕，赤光照室，有聲如爐炭之裂，星火四迸。
value.en: On the night he was born, a crimson glow filled the room, charcoal seemed to crackle in the brazier, and sparks burst outward on every side.
value.literal: On the night of his birth, red light filled the chamber; there was a sound like charcoal splitting in a brazier, and sparks flew in all directions.

value.zh: 司天上言：「今國家建號，以木德代水，準經法國以姓墓為臘，請以未日為臘。」
value.en: The Directorate of Astronomy submitted: "Now that the state has been founded, Wood replaces Water as the ruling element. By canonical law the La festival follows the tomb day of the dynastic surname — we request that the wei day be observed as La."
value.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy submitted a memorial saying: "Now that the state has established its title, Wood virtue replaces Water; according to canonical law the state takes the surname tomb day as the La festival — we request that the wei day be taken as La."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The request was approved.
value.literal: The request was approved.

value.zh: 時議者曰：「昔武王勝殷，歲集於房，國家受命，金、木集於房。
value.en: Commentators of the time said: "When King Wu conquered Yin, the year star gathered in Fang; when the state received the Mandate, Metal and Wood gathered there as well.
value.literal: Commentators of the time said: "In antiquity when King Wu conquered Yin, the year star gathered in Fang; when the state received the Mandate, Metal and Wood gathered in Fang.

value.zh: 文王厄羑裏，而卦遇明夷，帝脫於鄴，大衍之數，復得明夷，則周為國號，符於文、武矣。」
value.en: King Wen suffered at Youli and drew the hexagram Mingyi; the Emperor escaped at Ye and the Great Evolution numbers again yielded Mingyi — thus the state title Zhou accorded with King Wen and King Wu."
value.literal: King Wen suffered hardship at Youli, and the hexagram encountered Mingyi; the Emperor escaped at Ye, and in the numbers of the Great Evolution Mingyi was obtained again — thus Zhou as the state title accorded with Wen and Wu."

value.zh: 先是，丁未年夏六月，土、金、木、火四星聚於張，占者雲，當有帝王興於周者。
value.en: Earlier, in the sixth month of summer in the dingwei year, the Earth, Metal, Wood, and Fire stars gathered in Zhang; diviners declared that an emperor would rise under the name Zhou.
value.literal: Earlier, in summer, the sixth month of the dingwei year, Earth, Metal, Wood, and Fire stars gathered in Zhang; diviners said that an emperor or king would rise in Zhou.

value.zh: 故漢祖建國，由平陽、陜服趨洛陽以應之，及隱帝將嗣位，封周王以符其事。
value.en: Therefore when Han's founder established the dynasty, he moved from Pingyang and Shanfu toward Luoyang to fulfill the omen; when Emperor Yin was about to succeed, he enfeoffed a Prince of Zhou to match it.
value.literal: Therefore when Han's ancestor established the state, he moved from Pingyang and Shanfu toward Luoyang to accord with it; when Emperor Yin was about to succeed the throne, he enfeoffed the Prince of Zhou to match the matter.

value.zh: 而帝以姬虢之胄，復繼宗周，而天下之契炳然矣。
value.en: Now the Emperor, as a scion of Ji and Guo, has restored the Zhou line — and Heaven's design for the realm stands plain.
value.literal: Yet the Emperor, as a scion of Ji and Guo, again succeeded the ancestral Zhou — and the accord of all under Heaven was luminous.

value.zh: 昔武王以木德王天下，宇文周亦承木德，而三朝皆以木代水，不其異乎！
value.en: King Wu once ruled the realm under Wood; the Yuwen Zhou also claimed Wood — yet three dynasties all replaced Water with Wood. What a remarkable pattern!
value.literal: In antiquity King Wu ruled all under Heaven with Wood virtue; the Yuwen Zhou also inherited Wood virtue — yet three dynasties all used Wood to replace Water; is this not strange!

value.zh: 戊辰，前曹州防禦使何福進受宣權許州節度使，前復州防禦使王彥超受宣權徐州節度使，前澶州節度使李洪義受宣權宋州節度使。
value.en: On wuchen, former Caozhou Defender He Fujin was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Xu Prefecture; former Fuzhou Defender Wang Yanchao was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Xuzhou; former Chanzhou Military Governor Li Hongyi was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Songzhou.
value.literal: On the day wuchen, the former Defender of Caozhou He Fujin received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Xu Prefecture; the former Defender of Fuzhou Wang Yanchao received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Xuzhou; the former Military Governor of Chanzhou Li Hongyi received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Songzhou.

value.zh: 己巳，上漢太后尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
value.en: On jisi the Han Empress Dowager was given the honorific title Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
value.literal: On the day jisi, the honorific title Zhaosheng Empress Dowager was bestowed upon the Han Empress Dowager.

value.zh: 是日，詔有司擇日為故主發哀。
value.en: That day an edict ordered the relevant offices to set a date for mourning the former sovereign.
value.literal: That day an edict ordered the relevant offices to choose a day to proclaim mourning for the former sovereign.

value.zh: 〈（《五代會要》載原敕云：漢高祖為義帝發喪，魏明帝正禪陵尊號，一時達禮，千古所稱，況朕久事前朝，常參大政，雖遷虞事夏，見奪於群情，而四海九州，咸知予夙志。
value.en: (The Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties records the original edict: Han Gaozu proclaimed mourning for Emperor Yi; Wei Mingdi corrected the honorific of the Zen tomb — both timely fulfillment of ritual, praised through the ages. I long served the previous dynasty and regularly participated in great affairs. Though yielding Yu to serve Xia, I was displaced by public sentiment, yet all the realm knows my longstanding intent.
value.literal: (The "Institutional Compendium of the Five Dynasties" records the original edict as saying: Han Gaozu proclaimed mourning for the Emperor Yi; Wei Mingdi corrected the honorific title of the Zen tomb — timely fulfillment of ritual, praised through the ages; moreover I long served the previous dynasty and regularly participated in great affairs; though yielding Yu to serve Xia, I was displaced by public sentiment, yet the four seas and nine provinces all know my longstanding intent.

value.zh: 宜令所司擇日為故主舉哀，仍備山陵葬禮。）〉
value.en: Let the relevant offices choose a day to proclaim mourning for the former sovereign and provide full mountain-tomb burial rites.) (End of editorial note.)〉
value.literal: The relevant offices should be ordered to choose a day to proclaim mourning for the former sovereign, and also to provide full mountain-tomb burial rites.) (End of editorial note.)〉

value.zh: 辛未，有司上言：「皇帝為故主舉哀日，服縞素，直領深衣、腰绖等。
value.en: On xinwei the relevant offices submitted: "On the day the Emperor proclaims mourning for the former sovereign, he shall wear unbleached hemp, a straight-collared deep robe, and a waist mourning sash.
value.literal: On the day xinwei, the relevant offices submitted a memorial saying: "On the day the Emperor proclaims mourning for the former sovereign, he shall wear unbleached hemp, a straight-collared deep robe, a waist mourning sash, and the like.

value.zh: 成服畢祭奠，不視朝七日，坊市禁音樂。
value.en: After the mourning garments are complete and offerings performed, he shall not hold court for seven days, and music shall be forbidden in the wards and markets.
value.literal: When the mourning garments are complete and the offerings performed, he shall not hold court for seven days, and music shall be forbidden in wards and markets.

value.zh: 文武內外臣僚成服後，每日赴太平宮臨，三日止，七日釋服。
value.en: After civil and military officials complete their mourning garments, they shall attend daily mourning rites at Taiping Palace for three days, then cease; on the seventh day they shall lay mourning aside.
value.literal: After civil and military officials within and without complete their mourning garments, they shall daily attend mourning rites at Taiping Palace for three days, then cease; on the seventh day they shall remove mourning dress.

value.zh: 至山陵啟攢塗日，服初服，盾車出城，班辭釋服。」
value.en: On the day the mountain tomb is opened and the coffin sealed, he shall wear initial mourning dress; the shield carriage departs the city, and after the farewell ceremony he shall lay mourning aside."
value.literal: On the day the mountain tomb is opened and the coffin sealed, he shall wear initial mourning dress; the shield carriage departs the city, and after the farewell ceremony mourning dress is removed."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The memorial was approved.
value.literal: The memorial was approved.

value.zh: 壬申，前博州刺史李筠受宣權滑州節度使。
value.en: On renshen, former Bozhou Prefect Li Yun was proclaimed acting Military Governor of Huazhou.
value.literal: On the day renshen, the former Prefect of Bozhou Li Yun received the proclamation and was appointed acting Military Governor of Huazhou.

value.zh: 癸酉，樞密使、檢校太傅王峻加同平章事；
value.en: On guiyou, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jun, Grand Preceptor by special appointment, was made Grand Councilor;
value.literal: On the day guiyou, Wang Jun, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Preceptor by special appointment, was made Grand Councilor;

value.zh: 以前澶州節度使李洪義為宋州節度使，加同平章事。
value.en: former Chanzhou Military Governor Li Hongyi was made Military Governor of Songzhou and appointed Grand Councilor.
value.literal: the former Military Governor of Chanzhou Li Hongyi was made Military Governor of Songzhou and appointed Grand Councilor.

value.zh: 以滑州節度副使陳觀為左散騎常侍，鄴都留守判官王溥為左諫議大夫，並充樞密院直學士。
value.en: Huazhou Deputy Military Governor Chen Guan was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and Yedu Garrison Aide Wang Pu was made Left Remonstrance Grandee — both appointed Direct Academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
value.literal: Chen Guan, deputy military governor of Huazhou, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Wang Pu, administrative aide to the Yedu garrison commander, was made Left Remonstrance Grandee — both appointed Direct Academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

value.zh: 以元從都押衙鄭仁誨為客省使，知客押牙向訓為宮苑使。
value.en: Original-follower Chief Yamen Officer Zheng Renhui was made Commissioner of the Reception Bureau, and Reception Officer Xiang Xun was made Commissioner of the Palace Parks.
value.literal: Zheng Renhui, chief yamen officer of the original followers, was made Commissioner of the Reception Bureau; Xiang Xun, reception officer and yamen guard, was made Commissioner of the Palace Parks.

value.zh: 北京留守劉崇遣押牙鞏廷美致書，求劉赟歸藩。
value.en: Northern Capital Garrison Commander Liu Chong sent his yamen guard Gong Tingmei with a letter requesting Liu Yun's return to his post.
value.literal: Liu Chong, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, sent his yamen guard Gong Tingmei with a letter requesting that Liu Yun be returned to his frontier post.

value.zh: 帝報曰：「朕在澶州之時，軍情推戴之際，先差來直省李光美備見，必想具言，而況遐邇所聞，在後盡當知悉。
value.en: The Emperor replied: "When I was at Chanzhou and the army urged my elevation, I first dispatched Palace Attendant Li Guangmei, who witnessed everything — you must have heard the full account by now. What near and far have heard will all become clear in time.
value.literal: The Emperor replied: "When I was at Chanzhou, at the moment the army urged my elevation, I first dispatched the palace attendant Li Guangmei, who witnessed everything in full — you must surely have heard the full account; moreover what near and far have heard will all become known in time.

value.zh: 湘陰公比在宋州駐泊，見令般取赴京，但勿憂疑，必令得所。
value.en: The Lord of Xiangyin is presently at Songzhou and has been ordered brought to the capital. Do not worry — he will surely be properly provided for.
value.literal: The Lord of Xiangyin is presently stationed at Songzhou; he has now been ordered brought to the capital — but do not worry or doubt; he will surely be properly provided for.

value.zh: 惟公在彼，固請安心，若能同力扶持，別無顧慮，即當便封王爵，永鎮北門，鐵券丹書，必無愛惜。
value.en: As for you there, set your mind at ease. If you lend your strength in joint support without other concern, I shall at once enfeoff you as prince and charge you forever with guarding the northern gate — iron certificates and cinnabar writs will be granted without stint.
value.literal: As for you there, I earnestly ask you to set your mind at ease; if you can jointly lend your strength in support, with no other concern, I shall at once enfeoff you with princely rank, forever guarding the northern gate — iron certificates and cinnabar writs will surely be granted without stint.

value.zh: 其諸情素，並令來人口宣。」
value.en: All these matters shall also be conveyed orally by the envoy."
value.literal: As for all these circumstances, they shall also be orally proclaimed by the envoy who comes."

value.zh: 遣千牛衛將軍未憲充入契丹使。
value.en: He dispatched Qianniu Guard General Zhu Xian to serve as envoy to the Khitan.
value.literal: He dispatched Qianniu Guard General Zhu Xian to serve as envoy to the Khitan.

value.zh: 先是，去年契丹永康王烏裕寇邢、趙，陷內丘，及回，兀裕遣使與漢隱帝書，
value.en: Earlier, the year before, Khitan Prince Yongkang Wuyu had raided Xing and Zhao and captured Neiqiu. On his return Wuyu sent an envoy with a letter to the Hidden Emperor of Han,
value.literal: Previously, in the previous year the Khitan Prince of Yongkang Wuyu raided Xing and Zhao, captured Neiqiu, and upon his return Wuyu dispatched an envoy with a letter to the Hidden Emperor of Han,

value.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹之攻內丘也，死傷頗多，又值月食，軍中多妖異，契丹主不敢深入，引兵還，遣使請和於漢。）〉
value.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that in the attack on Neiqiu Khitan casualties were heavy; a lunar eclipse followed, and strange omens multiplied in the camp. The Khitan ruler dared not advance further, withdrew his army, and sent an envoy to sue for peace with Han.) (End of editorial note.)〉
value.literal: (From the "Comprehensive Mirror": when the Khitan attacked Neiqiu, dead and wounded were many; moreover a lunar eclipse occurred and many strange omens appeared in the army. The Khitan ruler dared not press deep, withdrew his forces, and dispatched an envoy to sue for peace with Han.) (End of editorial note.)〉

value.zh: 使至境上，會朝廷有蕭墻之變，帝定京城，回至澶州，遇蕃使至，遂與入朝。
value.en: When the envoy reached the border, the court was convulsed by internal strife. After the Emperor secured the capital he returned to Chan Prefecture, met the arriving Khitan envoy, and entered court with him.
value.literal: When the envoy reached the frontier, the court was struck by internal turmoil; after the Emperor secured the capital he returned to Chan Prefecture, met the barbarian envoy arriving, and entered court together with him.

value.zh: 至是，遣朱憲伴送來使歸蕃，兼致書敘革命之由，仍以金酒器一副、玉帶一遺兀裕。
value.en: At this point he sent Zhu Xian to escort the Khitan envoy home, with a letter explaining the change of dynasty, and presented Wuyu with a set of gold wine vessels and a jade belt.
value.literal: At this time he dispatched Zhu Xian to escort the incoming envoy back to the barbarians, also sending a letter explaining the reason for the dynastic change, and presenting Wuyu with one set of gold wine vessels and one jade belt.

value.zh: 晉州節度使王晏殺行軍司馬徐建，以通河東聞。
value.en: Jin Prefecture Military Governor Wang Yan killed March Chief of Staff Xu Jian and notified Hedong.
value.literal: Jin Prefecture Military Governor Wang Yan killed March Chief of Staff Xu Jian and reported the act to Hedong.

value.zh: 又詔在朝文武臣僚，各上封事，凡有益國利民之事，速具以聞。
value.en: Another edict ordered civil and military officials at court each to submit sealed memorials on any matter benefiting state or people, reporting at once.
value.literal: Another edict ordered civil and military officials at court each to submit sealed memorials; whatever benefits the state and benefits the people, report quickly.

value.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：詔曰：朕生長軍旅，不親學問，未知治天下之道。
value.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records the edict: I was reared in the army and never pursued learning myself; I do not know how to govern the realm.
value.literal: (From the "Comprehensive Mirror": the edict stated: I was reared in the army and did not personally pursue learning; I do not know the Way of governing all under heaven.

value.zh: 文武官有益國利民之術，各具封事以聞，咸宜直書其事，勿事辭藻。）〉
value.en: Any civil or military official with policies that benefit state or people should submit sealed memorials; write plainly of the matter and do not trouble over literary ornament.) (End of editorial note.)〉
value.literal: Civil and military officials who have policies benefiting the state and the people should each submit sealed memorials; all should write plainly of the matter — do not trouble over literary ornament.) (End of editorial note.)〉

value.zh: 辛巳，鎮州武行德、晉州王晏、相州張彥成、潞州常思、邠州候章並加兼侍中；
value.en: On xinsi Wu Xingde of Zhen Prefecture, Wang Yan of Jin Prefecture, Zhang Yancheng of Xiang Prefecture, Chang Si of Lu Prefecture, and Hou Zhang of Bin Prefecture were all made concurrent Palace Secretary;
value.literal: On the day xinsi, Zhen Prefecture Wu Xingde, Jin Prefecture Wang Yan, Xiang Prefecture Zhang Yancheng, Lu Prefecture Chang Si, and Bin Prefecture Hou Zhang were all additionally appointed concurrent Palace Secretary;

value.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使、果州防禦使、檢校太保郭崇為洋州節度使、檢校太傅，典軍如故；
value.en: Palace Guard Cavalry Commander and Defender of Guo Prefecture Guo Chong was appointed Military Governor of Yang Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, retaining command of his troops;
value.literal: Palace Guard Cavalry Commander, Defender of Guo Prefecture, and Honorary Grand Guardian Guo Chong was appointed Military Governor of Yang Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, command of troops as before;

value.zh: 以侍衛步軍都指揮使、岳州防禦使曹英為利州節度使、檢校太傅，典軍如故。
value.en: Palace Guard Infantry Commander and Defender of Yue Prefecture Cao Ying was appointed Military Governor of Li Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, retaining command of his troops.
value.literal: Palace Guard Infantry Commander and Defender of Yue Prefecture Cao Ying was appointed Military Governor of Li Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor, command of troops as before.

value.zh: 癸未，涇州史懿、延州高允權、滄州王景、永興郭從義、定州孫方簡並加兼侍中，鄜州楊信、同州薛懷讓、貝州王繼宏並加同平章事。
value.en: On guiwei Shi Yi of Jing Prefecture, Gao Yunquan of Yan Prefecture, Wang Jing of Cang Prefecture, Guo Congyi of Yongxing, and Sun Fangjian of Ding Prefecture were made concurrent Palace Secretary; Yang Xin of Fu Prefecture, Xue Huairang of Tong Prefecture, and Wang Jihong of Bei Prefecture were made concurrent Grand Councilor.
value.literal: On the day guiwei, Jing Prefecture Shi Yi, Yan Prefecture Gao Yunquan, Cang Prefecture Wang Jing, Yongxing Guo Congyi, and Ding Prefecture Sun Fangjian were all additionally appointed concurrent Palace Secretary; Fu Prefecture Yang Xin, Tong Prefecture Xue Huairang, and Bei Prefecture Wang Jihong were all additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

value.zh: 乙酉，華州王饒、河中扈彥珂、鄧州折從阮、邢州劉詞並加同平章事。
value.en: On yiyou Wang Rao of Hua Prefecture, Hu Yanke of Hezhong, Zhe Congruan of Deng Prefecture, and Liu Ci of Xing Prefecture were made concurrent Grand Councilor.
value.literal: On the day yiyou, Hua Prefecture Wang Rao, Hezhong Hu Yanke, Deng Prefecture Zhe Congruan, and Xing Prefecture Liu Ci were all additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

value.zh: 丙戌，幸西莊。
value.en: On bingxu the Emperor visited the Western Villa.
value.literal: On the day bingxu, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.

value.zh: 潞州奏，得石會關使王延美報，河東劉崇於正月十六日僭號。
value.en: Lu Prefecture reported that Shihui Pass Commissioner Wang Yanmei had notified them that Liu Chong of Hedong had usurped the imperial title on the sixteenth of the first month.
value.literal: Lu Prefecture memorialized that it had received a report from Shihui Pass Commissioner Wang Yanmei that Hedong Liu Chong on the sixteenth day of the first month usurped the imperial title.

value.zh: 丁亥，以前澶州節度使李洪義為宋州節度使，加同平章事；
value.en: On dinghai former Chan Prefecture Military Governor Li Hongyi was appointed Military Governor of Song Prefecture and made concurrent Grand Councilor;
value.literal: On the day dinghai, the former Military Governor of Chan Prefecture Li Hongyi was appointed Military Governor of Song Prefecture and additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor;

value.zh: 以曹州防禦使、北面行營馬步都排陣使何福進為許州節度使，加檢校太傅；
value.en: Defender of Cao Prefecture and Northern Expeditionary Chief Array Marshal He Fujin was appointed Military Governor of Xu Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor;
value.literal: Defender of Cao Prefecture and Chief Array Marshal of the Northern Expeditionary Camp for Horse and Foot He Fujin was appointed Military Governor of Xu Prefecture and Honorary Grand Mentor;

value.zh: 以博州刺史、北面行營右廂排陣使李筠為滑州節度使，加檢校太保。
value.en: Prefect of Bo Prefecture and Northern Expeditionary Right Wing Array Marshal Li Jun was appointed Military Governor of Hua Prefecture and Honorary Grand Guardian.
value.literal: Prefect of Bo Prefecture and Right Wing Array Marshal of the Northern Expeditionary Camp Li Jun was appointed Military Governor of Hua Prefecture and Honorary Grand Guardian.

value.zh: 戊子，有司上言：「準赦書，以晉、漢之胄為二王後，其唐五廟仲祀合廢。」
value.en: On wuzi the relevant offices submitted: "Under the amnesty, descendants of Jin and Han are appointed heirs of the two dynasties; the mid-year sacrifice at the Five Temples of Tang should be abolished."
value.literal: On the day wuzi, the relevant offices submitted a memorial saying: "According to the amnesty, descendants of Jin and Han are to serve as heirs of the two dynasties; the mid-year sacrifice at the Five Temples of Tang should jointly be abolished."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The request was approved.
value.literal: It was ordered.

value.zh: 庚寅，宗正寺奏：「請以晉、漢故事，遷漢七廟神主入升平宮，行仲享之禮，以漢宗子為三獻。」
value.en: On gengyin the Office of the Imperial Clan submitted: "Following Jin and Han precedent, we request that the spirit tablets of Han's seven temples be moved to Shengping Palace for the mid-year offering, with a Han imperial clansman serving as thrice-presenter."
value.literal: On the day gengyin, the Office of the Imperial Clan submitted a memorial saying: "Following the precedents of Jin and Han, we request that the spirit tablets of the seven temples of Han be moved into Shengping Palace to perform the mid-year offering, with a Han imperial clansman serving as thrice-presenter."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The request was approved.
value.literal: It was ordered.

value.zh: 廣順元年冬十月己丑朔，宰臣王峻獻唐張蘊古《大寶箴》、謝偃《惟皇誡德賦》二圖。
value.en: On the jichou new moon in the tenth month of winter, Guangshun 1, Chief Minister Wang Jun presented two Tang-era illustrated texts: Zhang Yungu's Great Treasure Admonition and Xie Yan's Admonition on the Emperor's Virtue.
value.literal: On the jichou new moon of the tenth month in winter, Guangshun year 1, Chief Minister Wang Jun presented two illustrated works from Tang: Zhang Yungu's Great Treasure Admonition and Xie Yan's Admonition on the Emperor's Virtue.

value.zh: 詔報曰：「朕生長軍戎，勤勞南北，雖用心於《鈐》、《匱》，且無暇於《詩》、《書》，世務時艱，粗經閱歷，前言往行，未甚討尋。
value.en: The Emperor replied by edict: "I was raised in the military and labored north and south; though I studied the war manuals Qian and Kui, I never had time for the Odes and Documents; I have only a rough acquaintance with the troubles of the times and have scarcely explored the wisdom of the past.
value.literal: An edict in reply said: "I grew up amid armies and toiled north and south; though I applied myself to the military manuals Qian and Kui, I had no leisure for the Odes and Documents; the affairs of the age and their hardships I have only roughly experienced, and the words and deeds of former ages I have not much investigated.

value.zh: 卿有佐命立國之勛，居代天調鼎之任，恒慮眇德，未及古人。
value.en: You aided the founding of the dynasty and now regulate the realm in Heaven's stead; I constantly worry that my limited virtue cannot match the ancients.
value.literal: You have merit in aiding the Mandate and founding the state, and hold the charge of regulating the realm on Heaven's behalf; I always fear my slight virtue falls short of the ancients.

value.zh: 於是采掇箴規，弼諧寡昧，披文閱理，懌意怡神，究為君治國之源，審修己御人之要。
value.en: You have gathered these admonitions to guide my ignorance; reading them delights the spirit and clarifies the roots of rulership and the essentials of self-cultivation and governing others.
value.literal: Therefore you gathered admonitions and regulations to assist my dim understanding; reading the text and examining its principles delights the mind and settles the spirit, probing the source of governing the state as ruler and discerning the essentials of cultivating oneself and commanding others.

value.zh: 帝王之道，盡在於茲，辭翰俱高，珠寶何貴！
value.en: The way of kings is fully contained in these works—both texts are superb; no jewel could be more valuable!
value.literal: The Way of emperors and kings is all here—both writings are lofty; what treasure could be more precious!

value.zh: 再三省覽，深用愧嘉。
value.en: I have read them again and again and am deeply moved—both humbled and grateful.
value.literal: On repeated examination I am deeply moved to shame and approval.

value.zh: 其所進圖，已令於行坐處張懸，所冀出入看讀，用為鑒戒。」
value.en: I have ordered your illustrations hung where I pass my days, so that I may read them coming and going and take them as my mirror and warning."
value.literal: The illustrations you presented have been ordered hung where I walk and sit, so that passing in and out I may read them as a mirror and warning.

value.zh: 壬辰，潞州奏，巡檢使陳思讓、監軍向訓破河東賊軍於虒亭。
value.en: On renchen Luzhou reported that inspector Chen Sirang and army supervisor Xiang Xun had routed Hedong rebels at Siting.
value.literal: On renchen, Luzhou reported: Inspector Chen Siyang and army supervisor Xiang Xun defeated Hedong rebel forces at Sixiting.

value.zh: 癸巳，以刑部侍郎司徒詡為戶部侍郎，以左散騎常侍張煦為刑部侍郎，以給事中呂咸休為左散騎常侍。
value.en: On guisi Situ Xu moved from Punishments to Revenue; Zhang Xu took Punishments; and Lü Xianxiu became Left Regular Attendant.
value.literal: On guisi, Vice Minister of Punishments Situ Xu was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Zhang Xu was made Vice Minister of Punishments; and Secretariat Drafter Lü Xianxiu was made Left Regular Attendant.

value.zh: 甲午，絳州防禦使孫漢英卒。
value.en: On jiawu Jiangzhou defense commissioner Sun Hanying died.
value.literal: On jiawu, Jiangzhou defense commissioner Sun Hanying died.

value.zh: 辛丑，荊南奏，湖南亂，大將軍陸孟俊執偽節度使馬希萼遷於衡州，立希萼弟希崇為留後，將吏二千餘人，遇害者半，牙署庫藏焚燒殆盡。
value.en: On xinchou Jingnan reported turmoil in Hunan: Grand General Lu Mengjun seized puppet governor Ma Xi'e, exiled him to Hengzhou, and installed his brother Xichong; of over two thousand officials and troops, half were killed and the headquarters treasury was nearly burned out.
value.literal: On xinchou, Jingnan reported: Hunan is in turmoil; Grand General Lu Mengjun seized the puppet military governor Ma Xie and moved him to Hengzhou, installing Xie's brother Xichong as acting commissioner; of more than two thousand officers and clerks, half were killed, and the headquarters treasury was burned nearly clean.

value.zh: 乙巳，詔並吏部三銓為一銓，委本司長官通判。
value.en: On yisi an edict combined the Personnel Ministry's three selection boards into one, with the ministry chief overseeing all reviews.
value.literal: On yisi, an edict merged the Ministry of Personnel's three review boards into one, entrusting joint adjudication to the ministry's chief.

value.zh: 丙午，晉州巡檢王萬敢奏，河東劉崇入寇，營於州北。
value.en: On bingwu Jinzhou inspector Wang Wangan reported that Liu Chong of Hedong had invaded and camped north of the prefecture.
value.literal: On bingwu, Jinzhou inspector Wang Wangan reported: Hedong's Liu Chong invaded and encamped north of the prefecture.

value.zh: 辛亥，潞州奏，河東賊軍寇境。
value.en: On xinhai Luzhou reported Hedong rebel raids on the border.
value.literal: On xinhai, Luzhou reported Hedong rebel forces raiding the border.

value.zh: 乙卯，荊南奏，淮南遣鄂州節度使劉仁贍，以戰船二百艘於今月二十五日入岳州。
value.en: On yimao Jingnan reported that Huainan had sent Ezhou governor Liu Renzan with two hundred warships into Yuezhou on the twenty-fifth of this month.
value.literal: On yimao, Jingnan reported: Huainan sent Ezhou military governor Liu Renzan with two hundred warships, which entered Yuezhou on the twenty-fifth of this month.

value.zh: 丙辰，詔樞密使王峻率兵援晉州。
value.en: On bingchen an edict ordered Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun to march to Jinzhou's relief.
value.literal: On bingchen, an edict ordered Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jun to lead troops to relieve Jinzhou.

value.zh: 丁巳，以左衛將軍申師厚為河西軍節度使、檢校太保。
value.en: On dingsi Left Guard general Shen Shihou was appointed Hexi military governor and acting Grand Mentor.
value.literal: On dingsi, Left Guard General Shen Shihou was made military governor of the Hexi Army and Acting Grand Mentor.

value.zh: 師厚素與王峻善，及峻貴，師厚羈旅無依，日於峻馬前望塵而拜，會西涼請帥，帝令擇之，無欲去者，峻乃以師厚奏之，師厚亦欣然求往，尋自前鎮將授左衛將軍、檢校工部尚書。
value.en: Shihou and Wang Jun were old friends; after Jun's rise, the homeless Shihou bowed to him in the dust before his horse every day. When the Western Liang post opened and no one wanted it, Jun nominated Shihou, who eagerly accepted—he had just been made Left Guard general and acting Works minister.
value.literal: Shihou had long been friendly with Wang Jun; when Jun rose to power, Shihou, destitute and without support, daily bowed to him in the dust before his horse. When Liangzhou requested a commander, the Emperor ordered a selection, but none wished to go; Jun therefore recommended Shihou, and Shihou also gladly sought the post; shortly before he had been appointed from his former post as Left Guard General and Acting Minister of Works.

value.zh: 翌日，乃有涼州之命，賜旌節、駝馬、繒帛以遣之。
value.en: The next day he received the Liangzhou appointment and was sent off with insignia, camels, horses, and silks.
value.literal: The next day came the appointment to Liangzhou, and he was sent off with banners of authority, camels, horses, and silks.

value.zh: 十二月丙戌，權武平軍留後劉言遣牙將張崇嗣入奏，於十月十三日，與節度副使王進逵、行軍司馬何敬貞、指揮使周行逢等，同共部領戰棹，攻收湖南，偽節度使邊鎬當夜出奔，王進逵等已入潭州。
value.en: On bingxu in the twelfth month acting Wuiping deputy Liu Yan sent adjutant Zhang Chongsi to report: on the thirteenth of the tenth month he, vice governor Wang Jinkui, chief of staff He Jingzhen, commander Zhou Xingfeng, and others led war boats to retake Hunan; puppet governor Bian Hao fled that night and Wang Jinkui entered Tanzhou.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingxu, Liu Yan, acting deputy of the Wuiping Army, sent adjutant general Zhang Chongsi to report to court that on the thirteenth day of the tenth month, together with vice military governor Wang Jinkui, campaign chief of staff He Jingzhen, commander Zhou Xingfeng, and others, they jointly led war boats, attacked and recovered Hunan; the puppet military governor Bian Hao fled that same night, and Wang Jinkui and the others had already entered Tan Prefecture.

value.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王逵傳》：逵，朗州武陵人，或名進逵。
value.en: (Per the Chronicles of the Nine States biography of Wang Kui: Kui was from Wuling in Langzhou, also known as Jinkui.
value.literal: (Chronicles of the Nine States, Biography of Wang Kui: Kui was a native of Wuling in Lang Prefecture, also called Jinkui.

value.zh: 邊鎬為武安軍節度使，召劉言入覲，言不行，謀於逵曰：「江南召我，不往，必加兵於我矣，為之奈何！」
value.en: Bian Hao, Wu'an Army governor, summoned Liu Yan to court; Yan refused and asked Kui: "If Jiangnan summons me and I stay away, they will attack—what can we do!"
value.literal: Bian Hao served as military governor of the Wu'an Army and summoned Liu Yan to court for an audience; Yan did not go and consulted Kui, saying: "The Jiangnan court summons me—if I do not go, they will surely send troops against me. What is to be done!

value.zh: 逵曰：「鎬之此來，以制置潭、朗為名，公如速行，正入其算。
value.en: Kui replied: "Hao's mission is to control Tan and Lang—if you hurry to court, you play into his hand.
value.literal: Kui said: "Hao comes on the pretext of administering Tan and Lang. If you go quickly, you walk straight into his plan.

value.zh: 武陵負江湖之阻，帶甲百萬，乃欲拱手臣異姓乎？
value.en: Wuling has rivers for defense and a million men under arms—will you meekly bow to outsiders?
value.literal: Wuling lies behind the barrier of rivers and lakes, with a million armed men—will you simply bow and submit to a surname not your own?

value.zh: 鎬新至長沙，經略未定，乘人心憤怒，引兵攻鎬，可一鼓而擒也。」
value.en: Hao has just reached Changsha and is unsettled—strike while men are angry, attack Hao, and you can take him in one rush."
value.literal: Hao has newly reached Changsha and his control is not yet settled; seize this moment while hearts are angry, lead troops to attack Hao, and he can be taken in a single assault."

value.zh: 言然之，乃遣與何景真等同起兵於武陵，號十指揮使，以攻邊鎬。
value.en: Yan agreed and dispatched him with He Jingzhen and others to raise troops at Wuling under the title Ten-Command Commander, to attack Bian Hao.
value.literal: Yan agreed, then sent him together with He Jingzhen and others to raise troops at Wuling, styling themselves Ten-Command Commanders to attack Bian Hao.

value.zh: 逵率舟師南上，至長沙，邊鎬大駭，以所部奔歸江南，諸州屯守皆罷之，盡復湖外之地。）〉
value.en: Kui led his fleet south to Changsha; terrified, Bian Hao fled with his troops back to Jiangnan, garrisons in every prefecture were withdrawn, and all territory beyond the lakes was recovered.)〉
value.literal: Kui led a fleet south to Changsha; Bian Hao was greatly terrified, fled with his division back to Jiangnan, garrison posts in all prefectures were abolished, and all lands beyond the lakes were recovered.)〉

value.zh: 癸巳，太子太師致仕安叔千卒。
value.en: On guisi, An Shuqian, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, died.
value.literal: On guisi, retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent An Shuqian died.

value.zh: 甲午，詔今後諸侯入朝，不得進奉買宴。
value.en: On jiawu, an edict forbade feudatory lords who came to court from presenting tribute to purchase banquets.
value.literal: On jiawu, an edict said that hereafter when feudatory lords came to court they might not present tribute to purchase banquets.

value.zh: 丁酉，皇子澶州節度使榮落起復，加同平章事。
value.en: On dingyou, Prince Rong, military governor of Cao Prefecture, left mourning restoration and was appointed co-equal Grand Councilor.
value.literal: On dingyou, Prince Rong, military governor of Cao Prefecture, left mourning restoration and was made co-equal Grand Councilor.

value.zh: 戊戌，太子少傅致仕王延卒。
value.en: On wuxu, Wang Yan, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, died.
value.literal: On wuxu, retired Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wang Yan died.

value.zh: 壬寅，幸西莊。
value.en: On renyin, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.
value.literal: On renyin, the Emperor visited the Western Villa.

value.zh: 乙巳，以端明殿學士顏衎權知開封府事。
value.en: On yisi, Palace Attendant Academician Yan Kan was appointed acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
value.literal: On yisi, Palace Attendant Academician Yan Kan was made acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs.

value.zh: 御史臺奏：「請改左右衛復為左右屯衛。」
value.en: The Censorate submitted: "We request that the Left and Right Guards be restored to the Left and Right Garrison Guards."
value.literal: The Censorate submitted: "We request that the Left and Right Guards be changed back to the Left and Right Garrison Guards.

value.zh: 從之，避御名也。
value.en: The request was granted, to avoid the imperial taboo name.
value.literal: The request was granted, to avoid the imperial taboo name.

value.zh: 是冬無雪。
value.en: That winter brought no snow.
value.literal: That winter there was no snow.

value.zh: 南齊書卷第三 本紀第三
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3

value.zh: 是月，上不豫，徙御延昌殿，乘輿始登階，而殿屋鳴吒，上惡之。
value.en: That month the emperor fell ill and moved to Yan-chang Hall. As he mounted the steps, the timbers groaned—the omen sickened him.
value.literal: That month the emperor was unwell; he moved his residence to the Yan-chang Hall. When the imperial carriage had just mounted the steps, the hall beams roared and creaked—the emperor hated this.

value.zh: 虜侵邊，戊辰，遣江州刺史陳顯達鎮雍州樊城。
value.en: Barbarians struck the frontier; day wuchen: Chen Xianda, inspector of Jiang, was sent to hold Fancheng in Yong.
value.literal: The barbarians raided the border; day wuchen: Inspector of Jiangzhou Chen Xianda was sent to garrison Fancheng in Yongzhou.

value.zh: 上慮朝野憂惶，乃力疾召樂府奏正聲伎。
value.en: Lest court and country panic, he roused himself in his sickness and had the Music Office play the orthodox repertoire.
value.literal: The emperor, fearing anxiety in court and country, forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox pieces.

value.zh: 戊寅，大漸。
value.en: Day wuyin: the end drew near.
value.literal: Day wuyin: he approached the final hour.

value.zh: 詔曰：「始終大期，賢聖不免，吾行年六十，亦復何恨。
value.en: An edict said, "Beginnings and endings come to every man, sage or simpleton; I am sixty—what is there to regret?
value.literal: An edict said: "From first to last, the great term—even sages cannot escape it. I have lived sixty years; what is there to regret?

value.zh: 但皇業艱難，萬機事重，不能無遺慮耳。
value.en: Yet the throne was hard-won and the realm is heavy—I leave cares behind.
value.literal: But the imperial enterprise is hard, and the myriad affairs weighty—I cannot be without lingering cares.

value.zh: 太孫進德日茂，社稷有寄。
value.en: The Grand Heir grows worthier by the day; the altars have their heir.
value.literal: The Grand Heir grows in virtue day by day; the altars have one to rely on.

value.zh: 子良善相毗輔，思弘治道；
value.en: Ziliang knows how to assist—carry the policy of good government forward;
value.literal: Ziliang is good at aiding and supporting—think to expand the way of rule;

value.zh: 內外衆事，無大小悉與鸞參懷，共下意。
value.en: within and without, great affairs and small—take counsel with Luan and speak with one mind.
value.literal: inside and outside, matters great and small—all consult with Luan and share your intent.

value.zh: 尚書中是職務根本，悉委王晏、徐孝嗣。
value.en: The Masters of Writing are the root of government—leave them to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaosi.
value.literal: Within the Masters of Writing lies the root of office—entrust it wholly to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaosi.

value.zh: 軍旅捍邊之略，委王敬則、陳顯達、王廣之、王玄邈、沈文季、張瑰、薛淵等。
value.en: Border defense goes to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanmiao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest.
value.literal: The strategy of armies defending the border—entrust it to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanmiao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest.

value.zh: 百辟庶僚，各奉爾職，謹事太孫，勿有懈怠。
value.en: Every minister and clerk—keep your charge, serve the Grand Heir, and do not grow slack.
value.literal: All the hundred offices and the host of clerks—each keep your post, serve the Grand Heir faithfully, and do not slacken.

value.zh: 知復何言。」
value.en: I have said enough."
value.literal: What more is there to say?"

value.zh: 又詔曰：「我識滅之後，身上著夏衣，畫天衣，純烏犀導，應諸器悉不得用寶物及織成等，唯裝復裌衣各一通。
value.en: Another edict said, "When I am gone, dress me in summer robes and painted heaven-garments, with a plain rhinoceros-horn belt; no precious ware or brocade in the rites—only one set of lined robes and one of padded robes for the coffin.
value.literal: Another edict said: "After my consciousness is extinguished, on my body wear summer clothes and painted heaven garments, a pure rhinoceros-horn belt; all utensils must not use precious things or woven brocades—only one set each of lined and padded burial garments.

value.zh: 常所服身刀長短二口鐵環者，隨我入梓宮。
value.en: The two iron-ringed knives I wore at my side, long and short—bury them with me.
value.literal: The personal knives I usually wear, long and short, two with iron rings—let them enter the inner coffin with me.

value.zh: 祭敬之典，本在因心，東鄰殺牛，不如西家禴祭。
value.en: Sacrifice is a matter of the heart; the neighbor who kills an ox is outdone by the neighbor who offers a simple spring prayer.
value.literal: Sacrificial reverence lies in the heart; the eastern neighbor slaughters an ox, yet it is not as good as the western family's simple spring rite.

value.zh: 我靈上慎勿以牲爲祭，唯設餅、茶飲、干飯、酒脯而已。
value.en: At my spirit seat use no sacrificial beasts—only cakes, tea, dried grain, wine, and dried meats.
value.literal: At my spirit altar be careful not to use victims; set out only cakes, tea, dried grain, wine, and dried meats.

value.zh: 天下貴賤，咸同此制。
value.en: High and low alike—let the realm follow this rule.
value.literal: High and low throughout the realm—all follow this rule.

value.zh: 未山陵前，朔望設菜食。
value.en: Until the tomb is finished, on the new and full moon offer vegetarian food.
value.literal: Before the hill tomb is complete, on the first and fifteenth of the month offer vegetable food.

value.zh: 陵墓萬世所宅，意嘗恨休安陵未稱，今可用東三處地最東邊以葬我，名爲景安陵。
value.en: A tomb is a home for ages; I always thought Xiuan Tomb unworthy—bury me on the easternmost of the three eastern plots and call it Jing'an Tomb.
value.literal: The tomb is the dwelling for ten thousand ages; I have long regretted that Xiuan Tomb was not fitting—now the easternmost of the three eastern sites may be used to bury me; name it Jing'an Tomb.

value.zh: 喪禮每存省約，不須煩民。
value.en: Keep the funeral spare—do not burden the people.
value.literal: Funeral rites should always be kept spare—do not trouble the people.

value.zh: 百官停六時入臨，朔望祖日可依舊。
value.en: Let the ministers end the six watches at the tomb; new moon, full moon, and ancestral days follow custom.
value.literal: The hundred offices stop the six sessions of attendance at the tomb; on the new and full moon and the ancestral day follow the old practice.

value.zh: 諸主六宮，並不須從山陵。
value.en: Princesses and the palace women need not go to the tomb.
value.literal: All princesses and the six palaces—none need follow the hill tomb.

value.zh: 內殿鳳華、壽昌、耀靈三處，是吾所治制。
value.en: Inside the palace, Fenghua, Shouchang, and Yaoling—the three halls I had made my own.
value.literal: Within the inner palace, the three halls Fenghua, Shouchang, and Yaoling are quarters I had built.

value.zh: 夫貴有天下，富兼四海，宴處寢息，不容乃陋，謂此爲奢儉之中，慎勿壞去。
value.en: A man who owns the realm need not sleep rough; I aimed at the mean between show and spare—do not tear those halls down.
value.literal: To hold the realm and the wealth of the four seas—yet where one dwells and rests cannot be crude; I call this the mean between luxury and austerity; do not demolish them.

value.zh: 顯陽殿玉像諸佛及供養，具如別牒，可盡心禮拜供養之。
value.en: The jade Buddhas in Xianyang Hall and their offerings—follow the separate memorial and tend them faithfully.
value.literal: The jade Buddhas of Xianyang Hall and their offerings—as in the separate memorial, worship and supply them with full devotion.

value.zh: 應有功德事，可專在中。
value.en: Works of merit may be kept within the inner palace.
value.literal: Merit works that should be done may be concentrated in the inner palace.

value.zh: 自今公私皆不得出家爲道，及起立塔寺，以宅爲精舍，竝嚴斷之。
value.en: Hereafter neither court nor household may ordain monks, raise pagodas, or turn a house into a chapel—the ban is absolute.
value.literal: From now on, public and private alike may not leave home for the Way, erect pagodas and temples, or turn a residence into a cloister—all are strictly forbidden.

value.zh: 唯年六十，必有道心，聽朝賢選序，已有別詔。
value.en: Only at sixty, with a settled will for the Way, may worthies of the court be chosen in turn—as the other edict already provides.
value.literal: Only at age sixty, when the mind for the Way is sure, may court worthies be selected in order, as already provided in a separate edict.

value.zh: 諸小小賜乞，及閤內處分，亦有別牒。
value.en: Small gifts and favors, and orders for the inner quarters—see the separate memorial.
value.literal: Petty grants and requests, and dispositions within the inner quarters—as in the separate memorial.

value.zh: 內外禁衛勞舊主帥左右，悉付蕭諶優量驅使之，勿負吾遺意也。」
value.en: The inner and outer guards who have long served at my side—give them all to Xiao Chen, treat them well and set them to useful work, and do not betray what I mean you to do."
value.literal: The long-serving commanders and attendants of the inner and outer palace guards—entrust them all to Xiao Chen, treat them generously and employ them as fits, and do not betray my dying wish.

value.zh: 是日上崩，年五十四。
value.en: That same day the emperor died. He was fifty-four.
value.literal: That day the emperor died, aged fifty-four.

value.zh: 蕭景先
value.en: Xiao Jingxian
value.literal: Xiao Jingxian

value.zh: 高宗廢立，穎冑從容不爲同異，乃引穎冑預功。
value.en: When Emperor Ming carried out his depositions and enthronements, Yingzhou remained outwardly unmoved; the emperor therefore counted him among those who had aided the enterprise.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming deposed and enthroned emperors, Yingzhou was composed and made no show of agreement or dissent; therefore the emperor drew him in to share in the merit.

value.zh: 建武二年，進爵侯，增邑爲六百戶。
value.en: In the second year of Jianwu he was raised to marquis and his fief increased to six hundred households.
value.literal: In the second year of Jianwu his noble rank was advanced to marquis and his fief increased to six hundred households.

value.zh: 賜穎冑以常所乘白＜牜俞＞牛。
value.en: The emperor gave Yingzhou the white ox he habitually rode.
value.literal: The emperor bestowed on Yingzhou the white riding ox he habitually used.

value.zh: 上慕儉約，欲鑄壞太官元日上壽銀酒鎗，尚書令王晏等咸稱盛德。
value.en: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Wang Yan, Minister Over the Masses, and others all praised this as supreme virtue.
value.literal: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Minister Over the Masses Wang Yan and others all praised this as supreme virtue.

value.zh: 穎冑曰：「朝廷盛禮，莫過三元。
value.en: Yingzhou said: "Of all the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.
value.literal: Yingzhou said: "Among the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.

value.zh: 此一器旣是舊物，不足爲侈。」
value.en: This one vessel is an heirloom and hardly counts as extravagance."
value.literal: This single vessel is already an old object and is not enough to count as extravagance."

value.zh: 帝不悅。
value.en: The emperor was displeased.
value.literal: The emperor was displeased.

value.zh: 後預曲宴，銀器滿席。
value.en: Later, at an informal banquet, silver vessels covered the tables.
value.literal: Later, at a private banquet, silver vessels filled the mats.

value.zh: 穎冑曰：「陛下前欲壞酒鎗，恐宜移在此器也。」
value.en: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty once wished to destroy the wine ladle—perhaps the effort should have been directed at these vessels instead."
value.literal: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty formerly wished to destroy the wine ladle—I fear the effort should have been directed at these vessels instead."

value.zh: 帝甚有慚色。
value.en: The emperor was deeply ashamed.
value.literal: The emperor was deeply ashamed.

value.zh: 南齊書卷四十六‧列傳第二十七
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46 · Biographies 27
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46, Biographies 27

value.zh: 建武初，除西中郎長史，行事、內史如故。
value.en: At the beginning of Jianwu he was appointed Chief Clerk of the General of the Right Division, retaining his acting authority and post as Interior Administrator.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the General of the Right Division, with acting authority and Interior Administrator as before.

value.zh: 俄徵黃門郎，未拜，遷吏部郎。
value.en: He was soon summoned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, but before taking up the appointment he was transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
value.literal: Soon summoned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates; before taking appointment, transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 尚書令王晏選門生補內外要局，慧曉爲用數人而止，晏恨之。
value.en: Wang Yan, Minister Director of State Affairs, wanted his disciples appointed to key posts throughout the government; Huixiao appointed only a few and stopped, and Yan resented him for it.
value.literal: Wang Yan, Minister Director of State Affairs, selected his disciples to fill key posts inside and outside; Huixiao used only a few and stopped—Yan resented this.

value.zh: 送女妓一人，欲與申好，慧曉不納。
value.en: Yan sent him a female entertainer hoping to win his favor, but Huixiao refused the gift.
value.literal: Yan sent one female entertainer, wishing to establish goodwill; Huixiao did not accept.

value.zh: 吏曹都令史歷政以來，諮執選事，慧曉任己獨行，未嘗與語。
value.en: Under previous administrations the Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel had controlled appointments through consultation; Huixiao exercised his own judgment independently and never once spoke with him.
value.literal: The Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel under successive administrations had handled selection matters through consultation—but Huixiao acted by his own judgment independently and never once spoke with him.

value.zh: 帝遣左右單景雋以事誚問，慧曉謂景雋曰：「六十之年，不復能諮都令史爲吏部郎也。
value.en: The emperor sent his attendant Shan Jingjun to question him about the matter. Huixiao told Jingjun: "At sixty, I am not about to consult the Chief Clerk in order to serve as Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
value.literal: The emperor sent his attendant Shan Jingjun to reprove him on the matter; Huixiao said to Jingjun: "At the age of sixty, I can no longer consult the Chief Clerk in order to serve as Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.

value.zh: 上若謂身不堪，便當拂衣而退。」
value.en: If Your Majesty deems me unfit for the post, I shall shake out my robes and resign at once."
value.literal: If Your Majesty holds that I am unfit, then I should shake out my robes and withdraw."

value.zh: 帝甚憚之。
value.en: The emperor was deeply intimidated by him.
value.literal: The emperor greatly feared him.

value.zh: 後欲用爲侍中，以形短小，乃止。
value.en: Later the throne wished to appoint him Attendant-in-Ordinary, but his short stature caused them to reconsider.
value.literal: Later they wished to appoint him Attendant-in-Ordinary, but because his stature was short, they stopped.

value.zh: 出爲輔國將軍、晉安王鎮北司馬、征北長史、東海太守，行府州事。
value.en: He was sent out as General Assisting the State, Army Administrator on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an as General Guarding the North, Chief Clerk Campaigning North, and Administrator of Donghai, acting for both the princely headquarters and the province.
value.literal: He went out as General Assisting the State, Army Administrator on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an as General Guarding the North, Chief Clerk Campaigning North, Administrator of Donghai, acting for headquarters and province.

value.zh: 入爲五兵尚書，行揚州事。
value.en: He was recalled as Minister of the Five Divisions and acting governor of Yang province.
value.literal: He entered as Minister of War Five Divisions, acting for Yangzhou.

value.zh: 崔惠景事平，領右軍將軍，出監南徐州，少時，仍遷持節、督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、輔國將軍、南兖州刺史。
value.en: After Cui Huijing's revolt was suppressed, he was additionally appointed General of the Right Army and sent to oversee Southern Xuzhou; soon after he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Assisting the State, and Inspector of Southern Yan province.
value.literal: When the affair of Cui Huijing was settled, he additionally held General of the Right Army, went out to oversee Southern Xuzhou; before long he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs of the five provinces Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Assisting the State, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

value.zh: 至鎮俄爾，以疾歸，卒。
value.en: He had barely reached his post when illness forced him to return; he died soon after.
value.literal: Having reached his post only briefly, he returned on account of illness and died.

value.zh: 年六十二。
value.en: He was sixty-two.
value.literal: He was sixty-two years old.

value.zh: 贈太常。
value.en: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.
value.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

value.zh: 列傳第三十三齊高帝諸子下
value.en: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi, Part Two
value.literal: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Qi, Part Two

value.zh: 隆昌元年，為侍中，領驍騎將軍，尋加秘書監。
value.en: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and commanded the Valiant Cavalry; soon he was also Director of the Secretariat Archives.
value.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and commanded the Valiant Cavalry; soon he was also made Director of the Secretariat Archives.

value.zh: 及明帝知權，蕃邸危懼，江祏嘗謂王晏曰：「江夏王有才行，亦善能匿跡，以琴道授羊景之，景之著名，而江夏掩能於世，非唯七弦而已，百氏亦復如之。」
value.en: When Emperor Ming seized power the princely residences were in peril; Jiang Shi once told Wang Yan, "The Prince of Jiangxia has talent and conduct and excels at concealing his abilities; he taught the zither to Yang Jingzhi—Jingzhi is famous while Jiangxia hides his skill from the world. It is not only the seven strings; the hundred schools are the same."
value.literal: When Emperor Ming grasped power the princely residences were in peril; Jiang Shi once said to Wang Yan, "The Prince of Jiangxia has ability and conduct and is also skilled at concealing his talents; he taught the zither to Yang Jingzhi—Jingzhi is famous while Jiangxia hides his ability from the world. It is not only in the seven strings; the hundred schools are likewise."

value.zh: 鋒聞歎曰：「江祏遂復為混沌畫眉，欲益反弊耳。
value.en: When Feng heard of it he sighed and said, "Jiang Shi is again painting eyebrows on chaos—intending to help, he will only make things worse.
value.literal: When Feng heard of it he sighed and said, "Jiang Shi is again painting eyebrows on chaos—he means to help but will only make things worse.

value.zh: 寡人聲酒是耽，狗馬是好，豈復一豪于平生哉。」
value.en: I am devoted to music and wine and fond of dogs and horses—how could I change a hair's breadth from the life I have always lived?"
value.literal: I am devoted to sound and wine and fond of dogs and horses—how could I be a hair's breadth different from my whole life?"

value.zh: 當時以為話言。
value.en: At the time this was taken as a memorable saying.
value.literal: At the time this was taken as a saying.

value.zh: 常忽忽不樂，著修柏賦以見志，曰：「既殊群而抗立，亦含貞而挺正。
value.en: He was often restless and unhappy and wrote the "Fu on the Evergreen Cypress" to express his intent: "Standing apart from the multitude yet rising up, it holds to integrity and stands upright.
value.literal: He was often restless and unhappy and wrote the "Fu on the Evergreen Cypress" to express his intent, saying, "Standing apart from the multitude yet rising up, it holds steadfastness and stands upright.

value.zh: 豈春日之自芳，在霜下而為盛。
value.en: It is not that spring days are fragrant in themselves—it flourishes beneath the frost.
value.literal: It is not that spring days are fragrant in themselves—it flourishes under frost.

value.zh: 沖風不能摧其枝，積雪不能改其性。
value.en: Gale winds cannot break its branches; piled snow cannot alter its nature.
value.literal: Gale winds cannot break its branches; piled snow cannot alter its nature.

value.zh: 雖坎壇于當年，庶後凋之可詠。」
value.en: Though cut down in its season, its later withering may still be worthy of song."
value.literal: Though it may be cut down in its season, later decline may still be sung of."

value.zh: 時鼎業潛移，鋒獨慨然有匡復之意，逼之行事典簽，故不遂也。
value.en: At the time the imperial enterprise was shifting in secret; Feng alone was stirred with intent to restore the dynasty, but the acting record-keeper constrained him, and so he did not succeed.
value.literal: At the time the imperial enterprise was shifting in secret; Feng alone was stirred with intent to restore the dynasty, but the acting record-keeper pressed him, and therefore he did not succeed.

value.zh: 嘗見明帝，言次及遙光才力可委之意，鋒答曰：「遙光之于殿下，猶殿下之于高皇，衛宗廟，安社稷，實有攸寄。」
value.en: He once saw Emperor Ming and in passing mentioned that Yaoguang's talent and strength could be entrusted; Feng answered, "Yaoguang toward Your Highness is as Your Highness was toward Emperor Gao—guarding the ancestral temple and securing the state: the charge is real."
value.literal: He once saw Emperor Ming and in conversation touched on the idea that Yaoguang's talent and strength could be entrusted; Feng answered, "Yaoguang toward Your Highness is as Your Highness was toward Emperor Gao—guarding the ancestral temple and securing the altars of soil and grain: the charge is real."

value.zh: 明帝失色。
value.en: Emperor Ming turned pale.
value.literal: Emperor Ming turned pale.

value.zh: 三十一年春正月甲戌朔，以日食，不受朝。
value.en: Year 31, spring, jiaxu new moon: Gaozong canceled audience for the eclipse.
value.literal: Thirty-first year, spring, first month, day jiaxu new moon: because of a solar eclipse, court audience was not held.

value.zh: 丁丑，雷。
value.en: On dingchou, thunder rolled.
value.literal: Day dingchou: thunder.

value.zh: 丁亥，免湖州增丁所輸絹。
value.en: On dinghai, Huzhou was freed from added-household silk levies.
value.literal: Day dinghai: the silk paid by Huzhou for added registered households was remitted.

value.zh: 夜，風雷雨雪交作。
value.en: That night wind, thunder, snow, and rain came together.
value.literal: At night, wind, thunder, snow, and rain struck together.

value.zh: 辛卯，詔江、浙官民戶均輸和市絁帛。
value.en: On xinmao, Jiang and Zhe were told to share silk transport and market purchases equally among official and common households.
value.literal: Day xinmao: an edict ordered official and common households of Jiang and Zhe to share equally in transport and market purchase of silk.

value.zh: 壬辰，劉寶落節鉞、福建路居住。
value.en: On renchen, Liu Bao lost his command tally and was sent to live on the Fujian circuit.
value.literal: Day renchen: Liu Bao was stripped of his command tally and made to reside on the Fujian circuit.

value.zh: 丙申，大雨雪，給三衙衛士、行在貧民錢及薪炭，命常平振給輔郡細民，諸路監司決獄。
value.en: On bingchen, heavy snow brought cash and charcoal to palace guards and capital poor; Ever-Normal stores fed nearby counties; commissioners judged cases.
value.literal: Day bingchen: in great rain and snow, money and fuel were given to the Three Yamaz guards and poor people at the mobile court; the Ever-Normal Granaries were ordered to relieve needy folk in auxiliary commanderies; circuit commissioners were to decide cases.

value.zh: 己亥，放張浚、胡銓自便。
value.en: On jihai, Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were freed to their own devices.
value.literal: Day jihai: Zhang Jun and Hu Quan were released to go as they pleased.

value.zh: 庚子，禁淮南拘籍戶馬。
value.en: On gengzi, Huainan could no longer seize and register civilian horses.
value.literal: Day gengzi: Huainan was forbidden to seize and register household horses.

value.zh: 三月壬寅，更定金使入境接伴、館伴舊儀。
value.en: Third month, renyin: the court revised the old protocol for welcoming and hosting Jin envoys on entry.
value.literal: Third month, day renyin: the former protocol for welcoming and hosting Jin envoys entering the realm was revised.

value.zh: 癸卯，成閔遣統制杜彥救淮甯，擊敗金人于項城縣。
value.en: On guimao, Cheng Min sent Du Yan to relieve Huai'ning and beat the Jin at Xiangcheng.
value.literal: Day guimao: Cheng Min sent controller Du Yan to relieve Huai'ning and defeated the Jin at Xiangcheng county.

value.zh: 甲辰，罷扈從官吏賞典。
value.en: On jiachen, reward grants to retinue officials were abolished.
value.literal: Day jiachen: reward grants to officials of the imperial retinue were abolished.

value.zh: 乙巳，錄商、虢之功，加吳璘少傅、王彥為保平軍節度使。
value.en: On yisi, merits at Shang and Guo were recorded; Wu Lin was made junior mentor and Wang Yan Baoping military commissioner.
value.literal: Day yisi: the merits at Shang and Guo were recorded; Wu Lin was advanced to junior mentor and Wang Yan was made Baoping military commissioner.

value.zh: 戊申，吳璘復德順軍，又遣將嚴忠取環州。
value.en: On wushen, Wu Lin recovered Deshun and sent Yan Zhong to take Huanzhou.
value.literal: Day wushen: Wu Lin recovered Deshun army and also sent general Yan Zhong to take Huanzhou.

value.zh: 辛亥，命兵部侍郎陳俊卿、工部侍郎許尹經畫兩淮堡砦屯田。
value.en: On xinhai, Chen Junqing and Xu Yin were ordered to plan fortresses and garrison farms on both sides of the Huai.
value.literal: Day xinhai: Vice Minister of War Chen Junqing and Vice Minister of Works Xu Yin were ordered to plan fortresses, stockades, and garrison farms on both sides of the Huai.

value.zh: 癸丑，金人圍淮寧府，守臣陳亨祖死之。
value.en: On guichou, the Jin besieged Huaining; defender Chen Hengzu was killed.
value.literal: Day guichou: the Jin besieged Huaining prefecture; defender Chen Hengzu died in the defense.

value.zh: 甲寅，吳璘自德順軍復還河池。
value.en: On jiayin, Wu Lin returned from Deshun to Hechi.
value.literal: Day jiayin: Wu Lin returned from Deshun army to Hechi.

value.zh: 金人犯鎮戎軍。
value.en: The Jin attacked Zhenrong.
value.literal: The Jin attacked Zhenrong army.

value.zh: 丁巳，遣洪邁等賀金主即位。
value.en: On dingsi, Hong Mai and others were sent to congratulate the new Jin emperor on his accession.
value.literal: Day dingsi: Hong Mai and others were sent to congratulate the Jin ruler on his accession.

value.zh: 戊午，忠義軍統制、知蘭州王宏拔會州。
value.en: On wuwu, Loyal-and-Righteous Army controller Wang Hong, prefect of Lanzhou, took Huizhou.
value.literal: Day wuwu: Loyal-and-Righteous Army controller and Lanzhou prefect Wang Hong captured Huizhou.

value.zh: 金人陷淮寧府，統領戴規戰死。
value.en: The Jin took Huaining; commander Dai Gui was killed in battle.
value.literal: The Jin took Huaining prefecture; commander Dai Gui died in battle.

value.zh: 成閔歸自淮東。
value.en: Cheng Min returned from east of the Huai.
value.literal: Cheng Min returned from east of the Huai.

value.zh: 辛酉，金人攻原州。
value.en: On xinyou, the Jin attacked Yuan prefecture.
value.literal: Day xinyou: the Jin attacked Yuan prefecture.

value.zh: 丙寅，詔舉賢良。
value.en: On bingyin, the court called for men of worth and excellence.
value.literal: Day bingyin: an edict summoned men of worth and excellence.

value.zh: 陶穀，字秀實，邠州新平人。
value.en: Tao Gu, styled Xiushi, came from Xinping in Bin Prefecture.
value.literal: Tao Gu, courtesy name Xiushi, was a native of Xinping in Bin Prefecture.

value.zh: 本姓唐，避晉祖諱改焉。
value.en: The family had originally borne the surname Tang but changed it to evade the imperial taboo of the Jin founder.
value.literal: His original surname was Tang; he changed it to avoid the taboo name of the Jin founding emperor.

value.zh: 歷北齊、隋、唐為名族。
value.en: For generations under the Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang they had ranked among the great families.
value.literal: Through Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang they were a distinguished clan.

value.zh: 祖彥謙，歷慈、絳、澧三州刺史，有詩名，自號鹿門先生。
value.en: His grandfather Yanqian had served as prefect of Ci, Jiang, and Li, won renown as a poet, and took the sobriquet Master of Deer Gate.
value.literal: His grandfather Yanqian served as prefect of Ci, Jiang, and Li prefectures, had a reputation in poetry, and styled himself Master of Deer Gate.

value.zh: 父渙，領夷州刺史，唐季之亂，為邠帥楊崇本所害。
value.en: His father Huan had governed Yi Prefecture, but during the chaos at the close of the Tang he was slain by Yang Chongben, the military governor of Bin.
value.literal: His father Huan held the post of prefect of Yi Prefecture; in the turmoil at the end of Tang he was killed by the Bin military commissioner Yang Chongben.

value.zh: 時穀尚幼，隨母柳氏育崇本家。
value.en: Gu was still a child then and grew up in Chongben's house with his mother, Lady Liu.
value.literal: At that time Gu was still young; he followed his mother the Lady Liu and was raised in Chongben's household.

value.zh: 王祜，字景叔，大名莘人。
value.en: Wang Hu, styled Jingshu, came from Shen in Daming Prefecture.
value.literal: Wang Hu, courtesy name Jingshu, was a native of Shen in Daming.

value.zh: 祖言，仕唐黎陽令。
value.en: His grandfather Yan had served as magistrate of Liyang under the Tang.
value.literal: His grandfather Yan served as magistrate of Liyang under Tang.

value.zh: 父徹，舉後唐進士，至左拾遺。
value.en: His father Che passed the jinshi examination under Later Tang and rose to left remonstrator.
value.literal: His father Che passed the jinshi examination under Later Tang and rose to Left Reminder.

value.zh: 高錫，字天福，河中虞鄉人。
value.en: Gao Xi, styled Tianfu, came from Yuxiang in Hezhong.
value.literal: Gao Xi, style name Tianfu, was a native of Yuxiang in Hezhong.

value.zh: 家世業儒，幼潁悟，能屬文。
value.en: His family had long been devoted to learning; bright from childhood, he could already write essays.
value.literal: His family for generations pursued Confucian studies; from youth he was quick-witted and could compose essays.

value.zh: 漢乾祐中，舉進士。
value.en: During the Qianyou era of Later Han he sat for the jinshi examination.
value.literal: In Han's Qianyou era he was recommended for the jinshi examination.

value.zh: 王晏鎮徐州，辟掌書記；
value.en: When Wang Yan governed Xuzhou he recruited Xi as his chief secretary;
value.literal: When Wang Yan commanded Xuzhou he recruited him as chief secretary;

value.zh: 留守西洛，又辟河南府推官。
value.en: and when Wang held the western capital he also appointed Xi investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
value.literal: when stationed at Western Luoyang he again recruited him as investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.

value.zh: 坐按獄失實奪官，遷置涇州，會赦得歸。
value.en: He lost his post when a criminal case he handled proved unfounded; after being reassigned to Jing Prefecture he was able to return home when an amnesty was proclaimed.
value.literal: He was stripped of office for investigating a case that did not accord with facts, was transferred and assigned to Jing Prefecture, and upon a general amnesty was allowed to return.

value.zh: 周顯德初，劉崇入寇，宰相請選將拒之，世宗銳意親征，破崇高平，誅敗將樊愛能等，由是政無大小悉親決之，不復責成有司。
value.en: Early in the Xiande era, when Liu Chong raided the border, the chief minister urged sending a general against him; Emperor Shizong insisted on taking the field himself, won at Gaoping, and executed the failed generals Fan Aineng and others. From then on he decided every matter himself, great or small, and no longer held the regular offices accountable.
value.literal: At the beginning of Zhou's Xiande era, Liu Chong invaded; the chief minister requested selecting a general to resist him; Shizong was keen to campaign in person, crushed the enemy at Gaoping, executed the defeated generals Fan Aineng and others; from this all affairs great and small he decided in person, no longer charging the responsible offices.

value.zh: 錫徒步詣招諫匭上書，請擇賢任官，分治眾職，疏奏不報。
value.en: Xi walked to the public suggestion box and submitted a memorial urging the appointment of worthy men and a proper division of duties among offices; it went unanswered.
value.literal: Xi went on foot to the suggestion and remonstrance box and submitted a memorial requesting selecting the worthy for office and dividing governance of many duties; the memorial received no response.

value.zh: 世宗嘗令翰林學士及兩省官分撰俳優詞，付教坊肄習，以奉遊宴。
value.en: Shizong once ordered Hanlin academicians and Secretariat officials to compose lyrics for variety players, have them rehearsed at the Court Entertainment Office, and perform them at his banquets and outings.
value.literal: Shizong once ordered Hanlin academicians and officials of the two secretariats separately to compose variety-player lyrics, delivered to the Court Entertainment Office for drill, to serve banquets and excursions.

value.zh: 錫復上疏諫。
value.en: Xi submitted another memorial in protest.
value.literal: Xi again submitted a memorial remonstrating.

value.zh: 後為蔡州防禦推官。
value.en: He later served as investigating officer on the defense staff of Cai Prefecture.
value.literal: Later he served as investigating officer on the Cai Prefecture defense staff.

value.zh: 李光 許翰 許景衡 張愨 張所 陳禾 蔣猷
value.en: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, and Jiang You
value.literal: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, Jiang You

value.zh: 所方招來豪傑，以王彥為都統制，岳飛為準備將，而李綱已罷相。
value.en: Suo was just recruiting bold men, appointing Wang Yan overall commander and Yue Fei preparation general, when Li Gang was already removed from the chief ministership.
value.literal: Suo was just recruiting heroes, making Wang Yan overall commander and Yue Fei preparation general, but Li Gang had already been dismissed as chief minister.

value.zh: 朝廷以王圭代之，所落直龍圖閣，嶺南安置。
value.en: The court replaced him with Wang Gui; Suo lost his Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion title and was exiled to Lingnan.
value.literal: The court replaced him with Wang Gui; Suo was stripped of Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion and settled in Lingnan.

value.zh: 卒於貶所。
value.en: He died in exile.
value.literal: He died at his place of exile.

value.zh: 子宗本，以岳飛奏補官。
value.en: His son Zongben was given office on Yue Fei's recommendation.
value.literal: His son Zongben received an official appointment through Yue Fei's memorial.

value.zh: 周必大
value.en: Zhou Bida
value.literal: Zhou Bida

value.zh: 兼侍講，兼中書舍人。
value.en: He was also made lecturer-in-waiting and drafting officer of the Secretariat.
value.literal: He was concurrently lecturer-in-waiting and drafting officer of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 未幾，辭直學士院，從之。
value.en: Before long he resigned his Hanlin post, and the emperor assented.
value.literal: Before long he resigned the Hanlin Academy post, and the emperor assented.

value.zh: 張說再除簽書樞密院，給事中莫濟封還錄黃，必大奏曰：「昨舉朝以為不可，陛下亦自知其誤而止之矣。
value.en: Zhang Yue was again appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs. The supervisory secretary Mo Ji returned the appointment record. Bida memorialized, "Yesterday the whole court held this impossible, and Your Majesty yourself knew it was a mistake and stopped it.
value.literal: Zhang Yue was again appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs; the supervisory secretary Mo Ji returned the yellow record; Bida memorialized: "Yesterday the whole court held this impossible, and Your Majesty yourself knew it was a mistake and stopped it.

value.zh: 曾未周歲，此命復出。
value.en: Less than a year has passed, and the appointment has reappeared.
value.literal: Not yet a full year has passed, and this appointment has reappeared.

value.zh: 貴戚預政，公私兩失，臣不敢具草。」
value.en: When imperial kin interfere in government, both public and private interest suffer. I dare not draft the document."
value.literal: Imperial kin interfering in government — public and private both lose; your servant dares not draft the document."

value.zh: 上批：「王嚴疾速撰入。
value.en: The emperor annotated, "Wang Yan — draft it at once.
value.literal: The emperor annotated: "Wang Yan — draft it immediately.

value.zh: 濟、必大予宮觀，日下出國門。」
value.en: Mo Ji and Bida were given palace-temple posts and ordered out of the capital gate that same day."
value.literal: Mo Ji and Bida were given palace-temple posts and ordered to leave the capital gate that very day."

value.zh: 說露章薦濟、必大，於是濟除溫州，必大除建寧府。
value.en: Yue submitted an open memorial recommending Mo Ji and Bida. Mo Ji was then appointed to Wenzhou and Bida to Jianning Prefecture.
value.literal: Yue submitted an open memorial recommending Mo Ji and Bida; thereupon Mo Ji was appointed to Wenzhou and Bida to Jianning Prefecture.

value.zh: 濟被命即出，必大至豐城稱疾而歸，濟聞之大悔。
value.en: Mo Ji left as soon as he received the order. Bida reached Fengcheng, pleaded illness, and returned home. When Mo Ji heard of this he was filled with regret.
value.literal: Mo Ji, on receiving the order, departed at once; Bida reached Fengcheng, pleaded illness, and returned home; when Mo Ji heard of this he deeply regretted it.

value.zh: 必大三請祠，以此名益重。
value.en: Bida thrice requested a temple post, and his reputation grew all the greater for it.
value.literal: Bida thrice requested a temple post, and by this his reputation grew heavier.

value.zh: 志第十三 天文一
value.en: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One
value.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1

value.zh: 魏齊王正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。
value.en: Under Wei emperor Cao Fang, Zhengshi 1, fourth month, day wuwu: the moon crossed the first star at the eastern horn of Hairy Head.
value.literal: Wei, Prince of Qi, Zhengshi year 1, fourth month, day wuwu: the moon encroached on the first star at the eastern end of Hairy Head.

value.zh: 其年十月庚寅，月又犯昴北頭第四星。
value.en: That year, tenth month, day gengyin: the moon again crossed the fourth star at the northern horn of Hairy Head.
value.literal: That year, tenth month, day gengyin: the moon again encroached on the fourth star at the northern end of Hairy Head.

value.zh: 占曰：「犯昴，胡不安。」
